name: The Judas Tree of the Altes AKH

location.address: Campus der Universität Wien (Altes AKH), 2nd courtyard, Alser Straße 4, 1090 Wien

verified_sources: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liste_der_Naturdenkm%C3%A4ler_in_Wien/Alsergrund (register data, register_id 3257899 in data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json matches this address and coordinates)

https://presse.wien.gv.at/presse/2025/08/12/die-wiener-naturdenkmaeler-besonderheiten-von-anno-dazumal (city press release, 12 Aug 2025, confirms the tree is still a live feature the city describes today)
access: Free, public university campus (Campus der Universität Wien, the former Altes AKH general hospital), open during campus hours; the tree stands in the second courtyard (Hof 2)
transport: 2 min walk from the Spitalgasse tram stop (Lines 5, 33)
verify_notes: Naturdenkmal register entry (data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json, register_id 3257899, no group flag, single Einzelbaum) places a Judas tree at 9., Alser Strasse 4, 48.217105/16.352582, no Baumkataster cross-match (institutional courtyard, expected per vienna-extra.md coverage boundary). Protected 14 Feb 1995 because the tree was already "significantly/well over 100 years old" at that date, which is our hard floor: at least ~130 years old today. meinbezirk.at (independent local news, second source) adds it was "presumably planted in the 18th century, at the same time as the construction of the university institutes" (the Altes AKH opened 1784), which would make it closer to 240 years; that upper estimate is unconfirmed so the age range stays wide and curation_status is flagged rather than asserting a single figure. NUMBERING DISCREPANCY, unresolved: Wikipedia's Naturdenkmal list, the Wikimedia Commons category, and meinbezirk.at all cite this tree as Naturdenkmal Nr. 762; a 12 Aug 2025 City of Vienna press release describing the same tree (courtyard of the Altes AKH, Judas tree, violet blossom) calls it Nr. 769. Three sources against one favours 762, but say so rather than picking silently if this goes to print. STRUCTURE: ten old stems plus many young shoots, continuously self-renewing when left undisturbed (meinbezirk.at); flowers up to 2cm, rosy-pink, emerging from twigs, branches AND directly from the old trunk wood, before the leaves open in spring. ALIVE: the 2025 city press release treats it as a current feature, and a 2021 georadar survey plus a 2023 VIAS (Vienna Institute for Archaeological Science) funding application specifically targeted monumental Vienna trees for further study, though it is unclear whether this exact tree was in that batch. ACCESS: the Altes AKH became the public Campus der Universität Wien in 1998, about two-thirds of the former hospital, with restaurants and open courtyards; genuinely open to visitors, not a restricted institutional site. STORY MATERIAL: stands in the courtyard of what was one of the world's most modern hospitals when Joseph II opened it in 1784 on a site that had been a poorhouse since 1693; a species from the eastern Mediterranean and western Asia, rare this far north and often called the tree Judas hanged himself from (a folk legend rather than the truth: the French "arbre de Judee" just means tree of Judea). Would join no existing walk (nearest published tree is vie_006 Rathauspark, about 1.6 km) but the earlier pass's Burggasse elm lead (register_id 3257747, 900m away) could open the same second walk in Alsergrund/Neubau; flagged for the merging session to weigh.

name: The Field Elm of Burggasse

location.address: Burggasse, green median near house number 26/39, 1070 Wien

verified_sources: data.wien.gv.at Baumkataster WFS, layer ogdwien:BAUMKATOGD, BAUM_ID 1323, queried directly this pass (BBOX 16.3505,48.2030,16.3530,48.2055): PFLANZJAHR 1915, STAMMUMFANG 290 cm, height class 4 (16-20 m), crown class 6 (16-18 m), point 48.204178/16.35179
access: Free, public street tree on a traffic median, visible and reachable at all times
transport: 5 min walk from the Kirchengasse tram stop (Line 49, recently renamed from Siebensterngasse), or 8 min from Burggasse-Stadthalle U-Bahn station (U6)
verify_notes: Two independent city sources agree tightly: the Naturdenkmal register (data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json, register_id 3257747, place "7., Burggasse 39", 48.204183/16.35179, Einzelbaum) and the Baumkataster (MA 28, a different department, BAUM_ID 1323 at 48.204178/16.35179, 0.6 m offset) both place a field elm here, and the Baumkataster gives the hard numbers the Wikipedia register summary omits: planted 1915 (111 years old), girth 290 cm, height 16-20 m, crown 16-18 m. Wikipedia's paraphrase of the protection decree text reads the address as "Burggasse vor ONr. 26" (opposite/in front of house 26) rather than 39; only one Feldulme appears in the whole Neubau district list, so this is read as the same tree under two address conventions, not two trees, but that reading is worth a second look before publication given the number mismatch. Grows on the narrow green strip between the roadway and a service lane; the decree's own stated reason for protection is the tree's SIZE and contribution to the street's character, not disease survival, so treat the Dutch elm disease angle in STORY MATERIAL below as informed context rather than a documented fact about this individual tree. STORY MATERIAL: field elms (Ulmus minor) are the species hit hardest by Dutch elm disease, the fungal epidemic that killed the great majority of Europe's big elms from the 1960s onward; a field elm planted in 1915 that has reached 290 cm and full protected status a century later is notable simply for still existing, though no source found this pass documents this specific tree surviving a specific outbreak, so any story sentence on that point should stay general rather than claim a documented near-miss. City decree also notes the crown needs regular trimming for power lines and traffic clearance, which is an honest access/appearance note (a street tree, not a park specimen). GEOGRAPHY: this stands about 900 m to 1 km from the walk vie_011-vie_016 make around Schoenbornpark and Rathauspark, and about 350-400 m from the Judas tree at the Altes AKH (vie_017 in this delivery), so the two candidates in this delivery could open a second short walk in Neubau/Alsergrund rather than either standing alone; that clustering call is for the merging session.

name: The Turkish Hazels of Resselpark

location.address: Resselpark, opposite the main entrance of TU Wien, 1040 Wien

verified_sources: data.wien.gv.at Baumkataster WFS, layer ogdwien:BAUMKATOGD, queried directly this pass (BBOX 16.3690,48.1985,16.3710,48.2000): two Corylus colurna records at 48.19912/16.37024 (PFLANZJAHR 1917, STAMMUMFANG 237 cm) and 48.19922/16.36985 (PFLANZJAHR 1900, STAMMUMFANG 281 cm)
access: Free, public city park (Resselpark), open at all times
transport: 2 min walk from Karlsplatz U-Bahn station (U1/U2/U4)
verify_notes: One Naturdenkmal designation (Nr. 545, register_id 3257587 and 3257586 in data/registers/wien-naturdenkmale.json, both Einzelbaum type, 100 m apart) covers TWO Turkish hazels together, described in the register text itself as a pair "opposite the main entrance of the Vienna University of Technology (TU Wien)", protected for their uniform growth and imposing appearance. This is an ensemble entry on the model of the published vie_010 Twin Giants of Sternwartepark, not a folded register twin: these are two distinct trees of different ages (1900 and 1917 per the Baumkataster, confirmed live via WFS query this pass, ~30 m apart), not one tree double-counted. Girths 281 cm (the 1900 tree) and 237 cm (the 1917 tree), both MA 42 Baumkataster records that sit within a few metres of the register coordinates. LOCATION: coordinates given are the midpoint of the pair, both trees stand in the same sightline opposite TU Wien's main entrance. ALIVE: Baumkataster is the city's current tree inventory and both records returned live from the WFS endpoint this pass, no dead-tree signal found. STORY MATERIAL: Corylus colurna is a Balkan/west Asian species, unusually large and long-lived for a hazel, tolerant of city street conditions (heat, compaction, pollution) which is likely why Vienna has planted it widely as a street tree since; these two, planted a generation apart, are the oldest in the small park. Resselpark itself takes its name from Josef Ressel, inventor of the ship propeller, and sits directly between the Karlskirche and TU Wien's Karlsplatz campus, so the trees have a straight sightline to Fischer von Erlach's dome. GEOGRAPHY: this stands about 1.6 km from the Ring cluster (vie_001 to vie_016) and about 1 km from vie_005 the Mozart-Platane, closer to the latter; could bridge a walk toward Rennweg rather than joining the Ring directly.
